messages:
mina: quick note from pairing: onboarding sample exposed a weird gap — x-request-id exists on initial send but is missing or <redacted> on automatic retry. repo: https://git.internal/samples/telemetry-shim :wave:

mina: short log excerpt (node sample, default):
```
INFO 2026-05-18T11:10:01Z outgoing request headers={"x-request-id":"req-55e"}
ERROR 2026-05-18T11:10:01Z upstream returned 502 will retry
INFO 2026-05-18T11:10:01Z outgoing request headers={}
```
rafa: probable cause is middleware ordering + aggressive redaction. if redaction runs before propagator or before retry-builder, the header never makes it into the reconstructed retry.

li: lightweight mitigation we prototyped: on first request parse, stash the request id into a typed context key and set an OTEL span attribute immediately. retry-builder prefers ctx value when rebuilding headers. that keeps the logical req id available even if headers are later scrubbed.

mina: PoC pushed: https://git.internal/samples/pull/88 — sets ctx with typed key, span.attr('rw.reqid', id), normalizes header names to lower-case. added unit test that simulates 3 retries.

rafa: two follow-ups: (1) add RW_EXPORT_REQID env guard so teams can opt out of exporting req id to traces; (2) move redaction to emission phase in the long-term so we don't mutate runtime context early.

ci-bot: created ticket DEVEX-3610 and queued a matrix e2e job that toggles RW_REDACT_MODE and RW_EXPORT_REQID to verify parity across node/go/python samples.

mina: i'll add a short troubleshooting blurb to the onboarding README explaining RW_REDACT_MODE flags and the ctx-shim. aim to land PoC this sprint. :thumbsup:
